title: Graphing a Reflected and Shifted Cubic Function
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: Graph and analyze the function y = (1 - x)^3 + 2 by starting with the standard cubic graph y = x^3 and applying appropriate transformations.

steps.title: Factor Out -1 to Reveal the Reflection and Shifts
steps.explanation: Since (-u)^3 = -u^3, we can rewrite (1 - x)^3 + 2 as -(x - 1)^3 + 2. Thus the graph is y = x^3 reflected across the x-axis (or y-axis), shifted right 1 unit, and shifted up 2 units.
steps.why: Odd powers satisfy (-u)^3 = -u^3, so horizontal and vertical reflections of y = x^3 coincide.

steps.title: Identify the Inflection Point, Monotonicity, Domain, and Range
steps.explanation: The inflection point is at (1, 2), and because of the reflection, the curve decreases from +infinity on the left to -infinity on the right.
steps.why: Negating the leading cubic term reverses the monotonicity from increasing to decreasing.

steps.title: Find the Intercepts and Guide Points
steps.explanation: The curve descends through the y-intercept (0, 3), passes through its inflection point (1, 2) and (2, 1), and crosses the x-axis at x = 1 + cbrt(2).
steps.why: Setting (1 - x)^3 + 2 = 0 gives 1 - x = -cbrt(2), or x = 1 + cbrt(2).
